jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in Behavioral and Experimental Economics
jobs.description:
About the position
NHH in Bergen, Norway, invites applications for a postdoctoral position in behavioral and experimental economics at the Department of Economics, as part of the FAIR Markets research project funded by the European Research Council (Project 101267064). The duration of the position is three years.The postdoctoral position offers a unique opportunity to join an ambitious research environment in behavioral and experimental economics and to become an integral part of the FAIR – Centre for Experimental Research on Fairness, Inequality and Rationality and the Department of Economics (FAIR) at the Department of Economics.The successful candidate will join an ambitious new research agenda on the moral foundations of markets and work closely with Bertil Tungodden and other researchers at FAIR and The Choice Lab on projects combining experimental methods, large-scale surveys, and rich administrative data to study how people evaluate the fairness and legitimacy of market transactions. The position provides substantial scope for intellectual contribution and for developing independent research within the broader FAIR Markets agenda.
 
We are looking for a highly ambitious and collaborative researcher with a strong background in behavioral and experimental economics and a particular interest in questions related to fairness, markets, and public policy. The successful candidate should have excellent analytical and technical skills. The ideal candidate will combine methodological rigor with creativity and a strong motivation to contribute to high-quality research aimed at publication in leading international journals.The department seeks ambitious candidates early in their careers. Applicants should hold, or be close to completing, a PhD degree in a business-oriented field such as economics or a closely related field from a recognised business school or university.
NHH offers
• Competitive terms depending on the level of competence/length of service.
• An academically stimulating working environment.
• A favorable membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) and good welfare benefits such as parental leave.
• Research funds for travel and conference participation, and a bonus system for publication in top international journals (up to NOK 200 000).
Note that public health care, public schooling for children, and most other public services are free in Norway. The city of Bergen has a mild, coastal climate and offers rich opportunities for culture and outdoor activities – as well as a family-friendly environment (explore visitnorway.com).
General information
The appointee must comply with the guidelines that apply to the position at any time.NHH emphasises diversity and encourages qualified candidates to apply for the position regardless of gender, age, disability and cultural background.In the assessment of applicants, international experience and qualifications will be emphasised. For the sake of gender balance at NHH, female applicants will be given preference in the event of equivalent qualifications among candidates.Applicants are requested to present a research statement with their application. The application should contain details of the applicant's scientific and pedagogical education and work experience. The application package, including a CV, certificates with grades, a maximum of 5 published or unpublished research papers, a complete list of published papers and papers in the pipeline, and any other relevant documentation, should be submitted through the Jobbnorge online portal. To open the application, please click 'Apply for this job'. For English version, go to the menu at the top right side.
 
Two or three reference letters (in PDF) must be submitted by the referees directly to NHH at hr-references@nhh.no, by latest 22 December 2026.

As part of the recruitment process, a background check may be conducted with the candidates' consent.

In accordance with §25 (2) of the Freedom of Information Act, information about applicants may be made public even if they have requested not to have their names entered on the list of applicants. Applicants will be notified if their request is not granted.

Enquiries about the position may be directed to:

• Professor Bertil Tungodden, by email: bertil.tungodden@nhh.no
• Administrative coordinator Mette Soltvedt, by email: mette.soltvedt@nhh.no
The deadline for applications is 22 December 2026. This date also applies to the submission of publications/written work.

jobs.occupation: Join NordicNeuroLab in developing electronics for the iMRI environment!
jobs.description:
NordicNeuroLab is expanding their work within interventional MRI (iMRI), and developing a communication system for these workflows.

 

As part of this initiative, we are building a dedicated engineering team, where we are looking for an experienced Hardware / Electronics Engineer to strengthen the iMRI team. In this role, you will take ownership of key technical challenges and help shape the solution, driving it from its current early stage towards a commercial product over the next two years.

 

What will you be working with?

Your work may include:

• Analog and mixed-signal circuit design
• Schematic and PCB design
• Embedded hardware and component selection
• Prototyping and technical concept evaluation
• Testing, measurement, troubleshooting and verification
• EMC/EMI and noise mitigation, including filtering, grounding and shielding
• Hardware and system integration
• Development with manufacturability and cost in mind
• Collaboration with suppliers, consultants and specialist resources when required
Because the system will operate in the MRI environment, you will work with technical challenges where the solution may not always be obvious from the outset. A hands-on approach to testing, experimentation and problem-solving will therefore be important.Some testing will take place in real MRI environments, so some travel should be expected.

 

Who are we looking for?

You have a relevant background in electronics, hardware engineering or a related discipline, combined with practical experience developing electronic products or systems.

 

Experience in analog and mixed-signal electronics is particularly interesting to us, ideally combined with schematic and PCB design. At the same time, the role requires technical breadth and an interest in working across disciplines.

 

You should also have strong English communication skills, both written and spoken, and work well in a collaborative, fast-paced development environment.

 

Most importantly, we are looking for someone with the drive to make things happen. Someone who takes ownership of a problem, digs into it and keeps moving when the first approach does not work.

 

We believe you will thrive in this role if you:

• Have a hands-on engineering mindset
• Take initiative and ownership of technical challenges
• Enjoy creating and developing new solutions
• Work independently while collaborating closely with others
• Are comfortable challenging technical decisions and discussing different approaches
• Are curious and willing to work outside a narrowly defined specialist area
• Can balance technical quality with progress, manufacturability and cost
 

Additional experience that would be valuable

Experience or familiarity with any of the following would be an advantage:

• Wireless systems, such as Bluetooth LE and Wi-Fi
• Audio electronics, including ANC and ENC
• RF
• Collaboration with suppliers, consultants and specialist resources
• Design for manufacturability
• Medical devices or regulated product development
• Electronics for demanding electromagnetic environments
• MRI-related technology
• AI-assisted engineering tools and familiarity with agentic AI
Experience with medical devices or electronics for the MRI environment would be highly relevant, but is not a prerequisite.

 

You do not need to tick every box. You may be particularly strong in one area and have broader experience or interest across others. We value strong engineering fundamentals, practical experience and the ability to learn and work across disciplines.

 

Why NordicNeuroLab?

You will join the iMRI initiative at an early stage of the development process and have the opportunity to influence important technical decisions..

 

You will work with challenging technology, where real clinical workflows and the MRI environment shape the engineering challenges.

 

NordicNeuroLab offers a flexible and collaborative working environment, with the opportunity to take on significant technical responsibility and contribute your expertise across different areas of product development.

 

For questions regarding this position, please contact Michelle Kolskår, Head of Sales at Folk AS.

Phone: +47 48 13 66 56 E-mail: michelle@folkas.com

 

Since its establishment in 2004, Folk AS has assisted both Norwegian and international companies in finding highly skilled professionals within technical and administrative disciplines for project-based, temporary, and permanent positions. This is what we do best, and where our expertise lies.

Our core values are: ethical, personal, committed, and flexible.

 

We see opportunities in your competence!

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Drone Detection and Interception Solutions
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Drones are increasingly considered as a security threat to society, including civilian critical infrastructure. Counter-drone systems must monitor the airspace as an integral part of a multi-layered air defence system, with functionality for detection, tracking and mitigating drone threats. Defending critical infrastructure such as railroads, bridges, power plants, power lines, airports, harbours, water supplies and more is challenging in a large country with complex geography and harsh climate. The PhD project will therefore research counter unmanned aerial systems (C-UAS) concepts and contribute to develop and test solutions that are specially targeting Norwegian needs.

The UAV-lab at NTNU has been one of the prime research environments for advanced aerial drone operations with 15 years of experience developing technology for drone autonomy and beyond-line-of-sight operations. The project will give you an opportunity to do work and research from theory, via simulation, to practice using and/or researching drone detection systems, interceptor drones and other technologies driven by advanced sensors, data communication systems, and artificial intelligence depending on skill, preference and prioritizations. In addition to the work at the UAV-lab you will collaborate with interdisciplinary team of PhD candidates on two other faculties.

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
The position is part of the project “Managing drone threats to critical infrastructure” as one of four PhD candidates.

A resilient society depends on safe and robust critical infrastructure, including the ability to withstand drone attacks. The war in Europe and hybrid threats have shown that such systems can be deliberately targeted using low-cost, commercially available technology, and the Government’s drone strategy identifies reducing vulnerability to hostile use of drones as the greatest and most urgent challenge. As threats and technology evolve rapidly, new uses of drones must be met quickly with adapted countermeasures.

The project aims to contribute to a more resilient society by developing knowledge and technological solutions to understand, manage and respond to drone threats and attacks against critical infrastructure.

The project is part of a larger effort of four projects funded by NTNU on A More Resilient Society.
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate.
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above.
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination.
• Participate in the research in the project “Managing Drone Threats to Critical Infrastructure”. and collaborate with the other PhD candidates and researchers in the project. 
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions.
• Collaborate with other PhD candidates, researchers and UAV operators at the NTNU UAV-lab.
• Carry out career-enhancing work as part of the project. This can include teaching duties.
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in control engineering, cybernetics, aerospace engineering, electronic systems, mechatronics, or equivalent. Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level. About the position
Starting date as soon as possible. The appointment is a full-time position and is for a period 6 months.

Place of work is Department of Geosciences, Section for Meteorology and Oceanography at Blindern, Oslo Norway.

The position is associated with the NORCLI (Nordic Climate History) project.

NORCLI is an interdisciplinary project led by Prof. Dominik Collet at the Department of Archaeology, Conservation and History and co-lead by Professor Kirstin Krüger at the Department of Geosciences, Section for Meteorology and Oceanography, at the University of Oslo. It is financed by the University of Oslo Thematic Research Group.

NORCLI is investigating Nordic Climate History: What happened the last time Nordic societies encountered rapid climate change? How did natural and social environments interact during the Little Ice Age (1300-1900), also in response to major volcanic events (i.e., 1690s, 1783-1783 Laki)? What can be learned from the ways people adapted to challenges that are in many ways similar to the ones we face today? The Nordic Climate History (NORCLI) research renders these fundamental questions researchable, using a novel 'socionatural' approach that integrates climatology and history and connects them to museology. NORCLI is working in three steps: (1) reconnecting available data from both the archives of nature (lake sediments, tree-rings, ice cores), climate physics (climate model data) and of society (historical records, material culture) with a focus on extreme events initiated by abrupt climate change in the last two millennia; (2) integrating interactions ‘from agriculture to culture’ bringing natural scientists and historians together; and (3) narrating results to a wider museum and societal audience.

The Quaternary Geology and Paleoclimate Researcher is expected to contribute to the working steps (1) and (2). The researcher shall be an experienced independent scientist within quaternary geology and paleoclimate specialized on varved lake sediments and their analyses in the Nordic countries. In addition, expertise on floods, hydroclimate variations, and natural hazards in particular in Norway during the Holocene are expected as well. As the candidate will be working closely with the other NORCLI positions on history, ice cores, tree rings, and climate modelling, we are seeking for a team player with an interdisciplinary background. Previous documented experience with the analyses of varved lake sediments in Norway next to other paleo climate proxies, and the historical archives on climate is required.

Mangfold og inkludering

jobs.occupation: Researcher / Postdoctoral Fellow in Microbial Ecology
jobs.employer_name: NORGES MILJØ- OG BIOVITENSKAPELIGE UNIVERSITET (NMBU) CAMPUS ÅS
jobs.description:
About the position
Do you want to take a leading role in turning a proven microbial concept into a scalable climate solution? At the Faculty of Chemistry, Biotechnology and Food Science, NMBU, we offer a three-year researcher/postdoc position in microbial ecology, starting in early 2027.

Agricultural soils are the largest human-made source of nitrous oxide (N₂O), a greenhouse gas almost 300 times more potent than CO₂. In a recent Nature paper, the Nitrogen group at NMBU showed that N₂O-reducing bacteria grown in biogas digestate can lower N₂O emissions from soil by 50–95%. This project, funded by the Grantham Foundation and the Platform for Agriculture + Climate Transformation, aims to make the approach cheap and widely applicable: we will design synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) that degrade crop residues such as straw and use them to fuel the growth of N₂O-reducing bacteria.

You will work alongside leading experts in the field. The Nitrogen group and the Microbial Ecology and Physiology group at NMBU have decades of experience in denitrification and N₂O biology and operate a robotized incubation system for high-resolution gas kinetics. 
 
The project leader brings expertise in the ecology of synthetic communities, and large-scale field trials and adaptation of the concept to US systems and substrates are run in close collaboration with Prof. Wendy Yang’s group at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

As the project’s lead experimentalist at NMBU, you will drive the lab work – from strain isolation to community assembly and N₂O measurements – with strong support from experienced colleagues. Large-scale production and field trials are carried out together with the wider team and parallel projects, giving your lab results a direct path to the field. You will also mentor students and have the opportunities to help shape new research directions and contribute to future funding applications.

This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career researcher to grow within a high-impact project and an experienced team. We look forward to your application!
Main tasks
The position is primarily experimental, and your responsibilities will include:

• Leading the isolation and characterization of bacterial strains that degrade complex plant polymers and enhance the growth yield of N₂O-reducing bacteria
• Designing and assembling synthetic microbial communities and testing them in microcosms
• Measuring N₂O reduction and assessing the performance of candidate communities
• Validating the best-performing communities in scaled-up cultivations
• Contributing lab results and expertise to field trials, including work with a field robot
• Mentoring master’s students and supporting the training of other team members
• Presenting results at international conferences and seminars
• Developing new research ideas and contributing to funding applications
• Leading and contributing to scientific publicationsCompetence
Required qualifications

• A PhD in microbiology, microbial ecology, biotechnology or a related field
• Documented wet-lab experience with bacterial isolation, characterization or cultivation
• Experience with independently planning and carrying out experimental research
• A strong publication record in international peer-reviewed journals, relative to career stage
• Good presentation skills, written and oral, in English
Qualifications considered an advantage

Experience with:

• Complex substrates such as straw or other plant biomass
• Isolation and characterization of bacteria
• DNA extraction from bacterial isolates
• Cultivation of microbial communities
• Denitrification, nitrogen cycling or anaerobic cultivation
• N₂O or other gas measurements
• Design and planning of wet-lab experiments
• Field trials
• Data analysis and bioinformatics 
Personal qualities

• Highly motivated and ambitious, with a high work capacity
• Analytical, with a strong ability to work independently and take initiative
• Ability to lead and coordinate practical research activities
• Good communication and collaboration skills
• Flexible and solution-oriented
Emphasis will be placed on personal suitability and on how the candidate’s experience fits the needs of the project. The overall assessment of qualifications will determine the ranking of applicants.
Remuneration and further information
The position is placed in position code 1109 Researcher (NOK 604900 – 966300) or 1352 Postdoctoral Fellow (NOK 604900 - 796600)depending on qualifications. For particularly well-qualified applicants, a higher salary may be considered. Appointment to a postdoctoral position aims to qualify for work in senior academic positions. 

A completed doctoral degree is required for appointment, and postdoctoral fellows are expected to participate in undergraduate teaching at NMBU. The position follows ordinary meriting regulations.
 
Interested in learning more about the position? Contact Prof. Åsa Frostegård, head of the research group, by phone at +4767232473  or by email at asa.frostegard@nmbu.no. 

General Information to applicants
Application
Send application electronically via the link "Apply for this job" at the top of this page. This will route you to the University's Web Recruitment System, where you will need to register an account (if you have not already) and log in before completing the online application form. 

Application Deadline: December 18, 2026

Your CV must be entered in Jobbnorge's CV form and not just included as an attachment. This is to be able to comply with the regulations in the Public Administration Act §15.
 
The following must be included in the application:

• Cover letter (max. 1 page), explaining your motivation for the position and how your experience fits the project. (please note that applications that lack a motivation letter clearly stating why the candidate is qualified and motivated for this particular project will be disregarded)
• Summary of research experience (max. 1 page), describing your most important research contributions and your own role in them.
• CV including a full publication list. 
• Up to five publications you consider most relevant to the position. 
• Copies of diplomas and other relevant certificates.
• Contact details for 2–3 references.
Applicants who are invited to an interview must be able to present certified copies of diplomas and certificates. 
About The Faculty of Chemistry, Biotechnology and Food Science
The Faculty of Chemistry, Biotechnology and Food Science (KBM) has about 180 employees, 80 PhD students and 500 BSc and MSc students. The faculty has 11 research groups within chemistry and biochemistry, microbiology and microbial gene technology, bioinformatics and data analysis, food science and nutrition. The Faculty has a state-of-the-art infrastructure for research and education: A biorefinery lab, proteomics platform, fermentation lab, a murine facility, platform for studies of microbial regulation of GHG release and a small-scale pilot plant for processing of food, incl. a microbrewery. Additionally, KBM has a strong competence in enzymology, fermentation and biorefining. KBM aims at a strong research position and collaborates in networks and research projects both nationally and internationally.  

For further information please follow this link: https://www.nmbu.no/en/faculty/kbm

Western Norway University of Applied Sciences (HVL) has a vacancy for a Postdoctoral Fellow in restoration ecology for a 3 year period
About the position:

We are looking for a highly motivated and talented postdoctoral fellow to join the Landscape, Ecology and Climate (LEC) research group at the Department of Civil Engineering and Environmental Sciences, at the Sogndal campus. The position is funded through the national, transdisciplinary research centre Landfutures, as part of its research area "Knowledge and worldviews". The Post Doc is a temporary, three-year position, but may be extended to four years with an additional year of teaching duties at the department. 

If you are interested in supporting sustainable land use by developing better prediction methods in restoration using advanced statistical modelling, and combine it with field work, this vacancy could be for you. 

The place of work for the position is campus Sogndal. 

Startingdate 01.05.2027
Key duties and responsibilities:
About Landfutures

Landfutures is an eight-year research centre for sustainable land and nature use (2026–2034), funded by the Research Council of Norway. The centre is led by Western Norway Research Institute and run jointly by Western Norway University of Applied Sciences, the Norwegian Mapping Authority, the Institute of Transport Economics, Nordland Research Institute, Ruralis Institute for Rural and Regional Research, the Norwegian Central Computing Centre and the Basque Centre for Climate Change in Spain. Landfutures aims to promote sustainable land use through transformative research and practice and intends to be a hub for research into profound societal changes in the way we use nature and land.

Background and research need

Sustainable land use acknowledges ecosystem restoration as a crucial strategy for halting biodiversity loss. Today, significant resources are invested in ecosystem restoration, yet our understanding of the long-term outcomes of restoration measures remains limited, partly due to insufficient monitoring and evaluation. 

 The Postdoctoral Fellow will explore methods for assessing restoration success of degraded ecosystems and supplement existing data from previous, long-term restoration studies with extra vegetation surveys. Emphasis will be placed on development of the ORBA (ordination regression-based analysis) approach. Concrete recommendations for how restoration projects can be monitored and evaluated shall be shared with practitioners. Ultimately, the work of the postdoctoral fellow will underpin evidence-based ecosystem restoration and contribute to Landfutures’ aim of strengthening sustainable land use and support well-functioning ecosystems.

Research environment

The postdoc fellow will be part of the LEC research group, an interdisciplinary group of ecologists and social scientists. We offer a stimulating, interdisciplinary academic environment. The postdoctoral  fellow will have their place of work and affiliation at campus Sogndal, and  work closely with the staff members of LEC, particularly Inger Auestad and Knut Rydgren.

The postdoctoral fellow will receive an annual stipend for conference participation, research visits, and equipment.

Through the transdisciplinary Landfutures centre, the postdoc will benefit from working with experts at the intersection of ecology, planning, political science, social anthropology and geography and in interaction with other Post Doc Fellows, PhD candidates and master’s students, as well as with relevant stakeholders. 
Qualifications:
Criteria for appointment to the position of postdoctoral fellow are regulated in Forskrift til universitets- og høyskoleloven.

Applicants must have earned a PhD in restoration ecology, vegetation ecology, or in a closely related field. Experience from botanical field work in Norwegian boreal ecosystems, and strong competence in floristics, including cryptogams, is mandatory. The candidate must have strong competence in (multivariate) statistical analyses and statistical modelling, particularly generalized linear models. A driver’s license is desirable. The applicant must have completed the PhD or have received confirmation of the date of defence before the application deadline

Applicants will be assessed primarily on the basis of:

• Relevant research experience and high-quality publications on restoration ecology 
• Competence and grades on completed course work
• Relevant experience in vegetation fieldwork in Norway or elsewhere in Scandinavia is an advantage.
• Previous involvement in relevant research projects
• A strong command of English and Norwegian or another Scandinavian language, both orally and in writing
Preference will be given to applicants with:

• Strong, practical programming skills in R or another programming language for data analysis
• Previous experience in supporting relevant MSc and BSc projects
• Previous experience in teaching relevant subjects
The following applicant characteristics will also be considered:

• Confidence in working independently as a researcher, and in cross-disciplinary teams 
• Ability to lead the writing of research papers, to initiate and advance research, and strong research and scientific leadership potential
• Potential for establishing relevant national and international research contacts
• Excellent communication and collaboration skills
• Capacity for dissemination and ability to positively contribute to advancement of nature restoration research at HVL
Applicants should explicitly address the qualifications and ranking criteria listed above in their application and provide sufficient documentation in their application to support the listed qualifications.

Educational competence

Educational competence is a requirement for all teaching and research positions.

If the applicant does not already have the educatinal competence required for a position as an associate professor, HVL shall facilitate that the competence is obtained during the period of employment.

Educational competence is documented by a pedagogical portfolio and a pedagogical CV.

Career plan

The person appointed shall, together with the institute, prepare a career plan that specifies the skills the postdoctoral researcher is to acquire. Competence goals shall be set both for the postdoctoral project and for any other career‑advancing work included in the position. The postdoctoral researcher will have access to career guidance.

Other career‑advancing activities may, for example, include teaching and teaching‑related work, development of Norwegian language skills and educational (pedagogical) competence, contributions to research communities, collaboration with public or private stakeholders, and more.
Application procedure:
Applications will be evaluated by an expert panel of three members.

Applicants are asked to submit their application and CV online. Please use the link “Apply for this job” (“Søk stillingen”).

The following documentation should be uploaded as an attachment to the online application: 

• A copy of the PhD thesis
• Copies of selected academic publications (no more than 15)
• A CV with a complete list of academic publications
• Diplomas and certificates
Applicants should indicate which publications or parts of publications should be given special consideration in the evaluation. If the documents submitted are not in a Scandinavian language or in English, the applicants must submit certified translations of these. The transcripts must specify the topics, the course works, and the grades at the bachelor`s and master`s degree levels.

Applicants with a degree from a country other than Norway, need to attach a certified translation of the diploma and transcripts of grades to English or a Scandinavian language, in addition to the original documents, if the original is not in any of these languages. It is required that the applicant encloses a recognition document showing that their degree is equivalent to a Norwegian bachelor’s degree, master’s degree, or PhD. You can read more about applying for recognition of foreign higher education here.

The Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir) offers an automatic recognition document for certain degrees from selected countries. If the applicant’s degree is covered by the automatic recognition, it will be sufficient to attach this document. Read more about automatic recognition here.

As the HK-dir application process may take some time it is recommended to apply to HK-dir as soon as possible. If you have not received a recognition document from HK- dir within the application deadline, please enclose documentation from HK-dir showing that they have received your application.

Applicants should note that the evaluation will be based on the documentation submitted electronically via Jobbnorge within the submission deadline. The applicants are responsible for ensuring that all the documentation is submitted before the closing date. It is of utmost importance that all publications to be considered in the evaluation are uploaded as an attachment with the application, since these are sent electronically to the expert panel. Applications cannot be sent by e-mail or to individuals at the college.
General information:
The appointment will be made in accordance with the regulations for State employees Law in Norway ("Lov om statens ansatte"). Organizational changes and changes in the duties and responsibilities associated with the position must be expected.

State employment shall reflect the multiplicity of the population at large to the highest possible degree. Western Norway University of Applied Sciences therefore aims to achieve a balanced age and gender composition and the recruitment of persons with diverse backgrounds.

Information about the applicants may be made public even though the applicant has requested not to be named in the list of applicants. The applicant will be notified if his/her request is not respected.

Short-listed applicants will be called in for an interview.

Western Norway University of Applied Sciences is subjected to the regulation for export control system. The regulation will be applied in the processing of the applications.
Salary:

• Exciting academic environment with the possibility of competence enhancement and development
• Opportunities for training within the working hours  
The Postdoctor position is compensated according to position code 1353 Postdoctor.

There is a compulsory 2 % deduction to the pension fund (see http://www.spk.no for more information). The successful applicant must comply with the guidelines that apply to the position at any time.

Om stillingene
Universitetet i Stavanger har ledig opptil fire stillinger som stipendiat i innovasjon, ledelse og markedsføring ved Handelshøgskolen UiS, Avdelingen for innovasjon, ledelse og markedsføring. Stillingene er ledig fra august 2027.

Stipendiatstillingen leder fram til doktorgrad og gir deg mulighet til å utvikle forskningskompetanse i et aktivt og stimulerende fagmiljø. Gjennom doktorgradsutdanningen opparbeider du kunnskap, ferdigheter og erfaring som kvalifiserer for videre karriere innenfor forskning, høyere utdanning og andre kunnskapsintensive sektorer.

De som ansettes tas opp på doktorgradsprogrammet i samfunnsvitenskap og forskerskolen i økonomiske og administrative fag (ECOBA). Programmet omfatter blant annet selvstendig forskningsarbeid, deltakelse i nasjonale og internasjonale forskermiljø samt forskningsformidling. Les mer om forskerutdanningen ved UiS på våre nettsider.
 
Stillingene er for tre år med ren forskerutdanning eller fire år med forskerutdanning kombinert med annet karrierefremmende arbeid. Dette avklares i rekrutteringsprosessen.Som stipendiat blir du en del av et ambisiøst, tverrfaglig og internasjonalt orientert fagmiljø innenfor  innovasjon, ledelse og markedsføring. Avdelingen er en av tre avdelinger ved Handelshøgskolen UiS med blant annet forskningssenteret Senter for innovasjonsforskning  og NHS Kompetansesenter er affiliert. Våre forskere publiserer i ledende internasjonale tidsskrifter og deltar i nasjonale og internasjonale forskningsprosjekter. Du får veiledning fra erfarne forskere, og gjennom forskerskolen ECOBA blir du del av et større ph.d.-fellesskap ved fakultetet. Vi samarbeider tett med nærings- og samfunnsliv i regionen og med forskningsmiljøer og legger til rette for forskningsopphold i utlandet i løpet av stipendiatperioden.
Forskningstema
Stillingene er knyttet til avdelingens tre fagområder: innovasjon, ledelse og markedsføring. Du står fritt til å utvikle ditt eget doktorgradsprosjekt innenfor ett av fagområdene, eller i skjæringspunktet mellom dem. I søknaden ber vi deg oppgi hvilket fagområde prosjektet ditt hører hjemme i.Innen innovasjon er det aktuelt prosjekter innen 

• innovasjonspolitikk og innovasjonssystemer
• geografiske perspektiver på innovasjon
• omstilling og innovasjonsdrevet transformasjon 
Vi imøteser særlig prosjekter som anvender nye tilnærminger til koblede registerdata, tekstanalyse eller prosess-sporing. 

Innen ledelse er det aktuelt med prosjekter som utforsker ledelse, organisering og kommunikasjon i et arbeidsliv i endring, blant annet hvordan kunstig intelligens og digitalisering av arbeid bidrar til å forme arbeidsoppgaver, roller, beslutningsprosesser og ansettelsesforhold. 

Slike problemstillinger kan også knyttes til temaer som ansvarlig ledelse, mangfold og inkludering. Prosjektene kan bygge på ulike teoretiske perspektiver fra ledelses-, organisasjons- og arbeidslivsforskning, og benytte kvalitative, kvantitative eller kombinerte metodiske tilnærminger.

Innen markedsføring ønsker vi særlig prosjekter innen markedsstrategi og kvantitativ markedsføring. Søkere oppfordres til å utforske avdelingens forskningsprofil og pågående prosjekter for ytterligere informasjon og inspirasjon.
Prosjektskisse
Som søker skal du utarbeide en foreløpig prosjektskisse for et doktorgradsprosjekt innenfor aktuelt forskningstema. Skissen vil inngå i kompetansevurderingen.

Prosjektskissen skal redegjøre for prosjektets problemstilling, relevans, samt teoretisk og metodisk tilnærming. Det forventes at skissen er et selvstendig og originalt faglig arbeid som reflekterer dine egne vurderinger og idéer. Dersom kunstig intelligens er benyttet i arbeidet med prosjektskissen, skal dette opplyses om og bruken beskrives kort.

Dersom du blir ansatt, vil prosjektskissen og prosjektets framdriftsplan videreutvikles i samarbeid med veilederne i løpet av de tre første månedene av ansettelsesperioden og danne grunnlag for den endelige planen for doktorgradsprosjektet. Mal for prosjektskisse finner du her.
Kvalifikasjoner
Du må ha en sterk faglig bakgrunn med femårig mastergrad innenfor økonomi og administrasjon, innovasjon, ledelse, markedsføring eller annet relevant samfunnsvitenskapelig fag, eller tilsvarende utdanning som gir grunnlag for å gjennomføre en forskerutdanning, fortrinnsvis av nyere dato. 

Karakter på masteroppgaven og veid gjennomsnittskarakter for masterstudiet må begge tilsvare B eller bedre. 

Dersom du har utdanning fra en institusjon med annen karakterskala enn A-F, ber vi deg legge ved dokumentasjon som viser hvordan karakterene kan sammenliknes med den norske karakterskalaen. Du kan bruke disse konverteringsskalaene til å beregne poengene dine for opptak.

Dersom du fullfører mastergraden våren 2027, er du også velkommen til å søke.

Mangfold og inkludering
Mangfold er en styrke ved universitetet. Ulike erfaringer, perspektiver og bakgrunner bidrar til bedre løsninger og et godt arbeids- og læringsmiljø. Vi ønsker søkere med ulike kvalifikasjoner, livserfaringer og perspektiver, og oppfordrer alle kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke, uavhengig av kjønn, alder, funksjonsevne, kulturell bakgrunn eller om du har hatt opphold i arbeidslivet. UiS legger til rette for ansatte i ulike livsfaser og for medarbeidere med behov for individuell tilrettelegging. 
 
I tråd med gjeldende regelverk vil minst én kvalifisert søker med funksjonsnedsettelse, hull i CV-en eller innvandrerbakgrunn bli invitert til intervju. Dersom dette gjelder deg, kan du oppgi det i jobbsøkerportalen. Les mer om ordningen her.  

Universitetet ønsker bedre kjønnsbalanse i stipendiatstillinger innenfor fagområdet og oppfordrer derfor særlig kvinner til å søke. Ved tilnærmet like kvalifikasjoner kan kvinner bli prioritert i samsvar med gjeldende regelverk.

UiS behandler bare søknader og vedlegg registrert i Jobbnorge.

Ansettelsesvilkår og videre prosess
UiS er underlagt sikkerhetsloven, og det forventes at ansatte utviser sikkerhetsbevisst atferd, og følger gjeldende sikkerhets- og eksportkontrollrutiner. Ved ansettelse vil egenskaper som pålitelighet, dømmekraft og lojalitet bli vektlagt.

Ansettelse som stipendiat er regulert i universitets- og høgskoleforskriften kapittel IV. Opptak til doktorgradsutdanningen er regulert i forskrift for graden philosophiae doctor (ph.d.) ved Universitetet i Stavanger.

Dine kvalifikasjoner for stillingen vil bli vurdert av en intern komité på grunnlag av dokumentasjonen registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristens utløp. På bakgrunn av komiteens vurdering vil aktuelle søkere bli invitert til intervju. Det vil også bli innhentet referanser for aktuelle kandidater. Les mer om ansettelsesprosessen på våre nettsider.
 
Doktorgradsarbeidet skal i hovedsak gjennomføres ved Universitetet i Stavanger. Det er en forutsetning at den som ansettes bosetter seg slik at vedkommende kan være til stede og tilgjengelig for fagmiljøet i ordinær arbeidstid.

Stillingen er kunngjort på både norsk og engelsk. Ved eventuelle motstridende opplysninger mellom tekstene er det den norske teksten som legges til grunn.
